events.title: Jamestown Massacre
events.description: Algonquian warriors launched coordinated surprise attacks on English settlements around Jamestown, Virginia. They killed 347 colonists, about a third of the colony's population.
events.significance: The attack set off years of brutal warfare between English settlers and the Powhatan Confederacy. It hardened colonial attitudes toward Native peoples in early Virginia.

events.title: British Parliament Passes the Stamp Act
events.description: Parliament approved the Stamp Act. It required printed materials in the American colonies, from legal documents to newspapers and playing cards, to carry a tax stamp.
events.significance: It was the first direct tax Britain levied on the American colonies. It sparked the protest slogan "no taxation without representation" and pushed the colonies toward revolution.

events.title: The Football League Is Formed
events.description: Twelve English clubs came together to organize regular competitive fixtures, replacing the haphazard schedule of friendly matches.
events.significance: It created the world's first professional football league. Its model of a season-long league table became the template for competitions around the globe.

events.title: The Arab League Is Founded
events.description: Representatives of several Arab states signed the Pact of the League of Arab States in Cairo. It created a regional organization in which each member state held one vote.
events.significance: The Arab League became a central forum for political and economic cooperation across the Arab world. It continues to shape regional diplomacy today.
